laws.rule: Consuming, producing or transporting alcohol is illegal in Nagaland. Drinking or possessing alcohol there can mean arrest without bail and 5 to 10 years' prison.

layers.process: The entire area of Nagaland is a Protected Area under the Third Schedule of India's Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit to enter or stay. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (the e-FRRO portal) or in the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; the permit is issued electronically. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there (born there, a parent or grandparent born and permanently living there, or ever a citizen), need the central government's prior approval. Smartraveller advises applying at least 4 weeks ahead; entering without a permit carries significant penalties.

zone-requirements.note: Smartraveller (updated 29 October 2026) still says the Ministry of Home Affairs has temporarily excluded Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland from the Protected Area regime. The 2025 Order, which replaced the 1958 Protected Areas Order, lists the entire state as a Protected Area, and news reports in December 2024 said the earlier exclusion had been withdrawn. Confirm with the e-FRRO portal or an Indian mission before travel.

items.text: Nagaland has total prohibition under the Nagaland Liquor Total Prohibition Act 1989. The state Excise and Prohibition Department's main work is enforcing it, by controlling the possession, sale, consumption, manufacture and transport of liquor. Liquor for military and paramilitary units comes in separately, through canteen stores and bonded warehouses at Dimapur.
